name: NCV8114ASN165T1G
title: 300 mA low-noise CMOS LDO regulator for automotive use
summary: The NCV8114 is a fixed-output CMOS linear regulator for loads up to 300 mA, running from 1.7 V to 5.5 V in a five-pin TSOP. Its ground current is 50 µA typical with no load and falls to 0.01 µA when EN is low; ripple rejection is 75 dB at 1 kHz and output noise 70 µVrms. It is stable with a 1 µF ceramic output capacitor, limits current and shuts down when hot, and the A versions pull the output to ground through 100 Ω while disabled. The NCV prefix marks parts qualified to AEC-Q100 and PPAP capable; outputs run from 1.2 V to 3.3 V in this family, the NCV8114ASN165T1G giving 1.65 V.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply input; needs a small capacitor to ground for the regulator to stay stable.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground for the supply and the output.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. Above 0.9 V the regulator runs; below 0.4 V it shuts down. An internal 300 nA pull-down holds it off when the pin floats.

pins.name: N/C
pins.function: No internal connection; may be grounded to help carry heat away.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Regulated output; a ceramic capacitor of at least 1 µF to ground keeps the loop stable.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The regulator with one capacitor at its input and a 1 µF ceramic at its output, both to ground. EN is driven by an on/off control: high runs the regulator, low shuts it down. Pin 4 has no connection.

parts.note: input capacitor; at least 1 µF X5R or X7R ceramic, placed at IN

where.IGND(IOUT): ground current at the operating output current

operation.text: Every part has a fixed output. A versions (NCV8114ASN...) carry the output discharge switch; B versions (NCV8114BSN...) do not. The family is offered from 0.9 V to 3.6 V on request, with 1.2, 1.5, 1.65, 1.7, 1.8, 2.5, 2.8, 3.0 and 3.3 V listed; the 1.5 V parts and the B parts at 2.8 V and 3.0 V are discontinued and not for new designs.
The part adjusts its quiescent current dynamically, which keeps it very low at no load; no-load ground current is 50 µA typical.

Use a ceramic X5R or X7R of 1 µF or more right at IN. Its ESR has no lower or upper limit, but ceramics are preferred for their low ESR and ESL. It gives AC noise riding on the supply a low-impedance path and limits the effect of input trace inductance and source resistance during sudden load steps; fast, large load steps may call for a bigger one.

Place a 1 µF X7R or X5R at OUT. The loop stays stable down to 0.22 µF of effective capacitance, which covers loss with temperature, DC bias and case size; small cases such as 0402 lose capacitance fast under bias. ESR has no minimum but must stay under 2 Ω. More capacitance and lower ESR improve load-step response and PSRR at high frequency. Tantalum is not recommended: its ESR is high and climbs in the cold.

EN below 0.4 V turns the regulator off for certain: the pass device opens, the input draws about 10 nA, and on A versions the output is pulled to ground through 100 Ω. EN above 0.9 V turns it on for certain and releases the discharge switch. A 300 nA typical pull-down inside keeps the part off when EN is left open; where enable control is not wanted, EN connects straight to IN.

Output current is limited inside to 600 mA typical, measured with the output 10 % below nominal. With the output shorted to ground the limit is 630 mA typical. Both work across the full input voltage and temperature ranges, and a short may last indefinitely.

Above about 160 °C die temperature the regulator switches off, and it switches back on once the die cools below about 140 °C. The feature guards against accidental overheating and does not replace proper heat sinking.

How much the part can dissipate depends on the board: pad layout, board material and ambient temperature set how fast the junction heats. Keep the junction at or below 125 °C. More copper on the pins lowers the thermal resistance.
The PMOS pass device has a body diode that conducts when VOUT is above VIN. Where that condition can persist, external protection may be needed.
Rejection between 100 kHz and 10 MHz can be adjusted through the choice of COUT and the board layout.
Turn-on time runs from EN going high until VOUT reaches 98 % of nominal. It depends on VOUT(NOM), COUT and TA; for VOUT = 1.2 V, COUT = 1 µF, IOUT = 1 mA and TA = 25 °C it is 90 µs typical.
Put CIN and COUT close to the pins and keep the traces wide for good transient response and regulation; 0402 capacitors keep the circuit small. Any exposed pad goes to GND by the shortest path.
